variants.name: Genomics
variants.description: Questions against the bundled synthetic Genomics sample (subjects, samples of 2023 and 2024, variants, calls and expression; invented data), each guarding a planted trap. Select its PostgreSQL datasource with a saved dataset containing the genomics tables and views; Settings, Testing Data loads both.

cases.question: Which five genes show the highest average alternate-allele fraction?
cases.intent: Rank genes by alt_read_count / total_read_count — two genuinely different measures — rather than by a ratio of a column with its own duplicate.
cases.notes:
read_depth equals total_read_count on all 5263 calls, so any fraction built from that pair is exactly 1.0000 for every gene and the ranking becomes alphabetical noise. A correct answer divides ALTERNATE reads by TOTAL reads; over the non-control samples the dataset's default filter keeps, all 40 gene means are still distinct, so the top five are unambiguous (MUTYH 0.5325, SCN5A 0.5068, SMAD4 0.5066, TSC2 0.4943, XIST 0.4921) with EGFR sixth on 0.4699 — SCN5A and SMAD4 sit 0.0002 apart but both are inside the five, and the symbol tie-break fixes their order. The reference also applies the allele_fraction metric's qualifiers (PASS calls, depth >= 20), which is part of why this is hard. The fractions are checked by the result set; the text check asks for the top gene. This guards the regression where the engine picked the similarly named column and reported a perfect fraction everywhere. trapSql divides read depth by total reads (the duplicate pair): verified 1.0000 for every gene, so its top five is alphabetical (APC, APOB, ATM, BMPR1A, BRCA1) against the reference MUTYH 0.5325 … XIST 0.4921.

Trap query (must return different rows): SELECT gene.hgnc_symbol AS gene, ROUND(AVG(call.read_depth * 1.0 / call.total_read_count), 4) AS mean_allele_fraction FROM genomics.variant_calls call JOIN genomics.samples sample ON sample.id = call.sample_id JOIN genomics.variants variant ON variant.id = call.variant_id JOIN genomics.genes gene ON gene.id = variant.gene_id WHERE sample.is_control = false AND call.filter_status = 'PASS' AND call.total_read_count >= 20 GROUP BY gene.hgnc_symbol ORDER BY mean_allele_fraction DESC, gene.hgnc_symbol LIMIT 5

Paraphrases: What are the top five genes by mean alternate-allele fraction? | Rank our genes by average alternate-allele fraction and give me the top five.

Moved from feat/engine-eval-loop (branch category ratio-trap, provenance hand).

expectedSql.postgres: SELECT gene.hgnc_symbol AS gene, ROUND(AVG(call.alt_read_count::numeric / call.total_read_count), 4) AS mean_allele_fraction FROM genomics.variant_calls call JOIN genomics.samples sample ON sample.id = call.sample_id JOIN genomics.variants variant ON variant.id = call.variant_id JOIN genomics.genes gene ON gene.id = variant.gene_id WHERE sample.is_control = false AND call.filter_status = 'PASS' AND call.total_read_count >= 20 GROUP BY gene.hgnc_symbol ORDER BY mean_allele_fraction DESC, gene.hgnc_symbol LIMIT 5

cases.question: Across high-confidence calls with at least 20 reads, what is the average alternate-allele fraction for each genotype, to three decimal places?
cases.intent: Divide alternate reads by total reads per call and average by genotype — not the duplicate read-depth column by the total, which is 1 everywhere.
cases.notes:
Verified against the live fixture (default filter applied, controls out; PASS calls with total reads >= 20): 3 rows — 0/0 0.022, 0/1 0.480, 1/1 0.950, the textbook shape (homozygous reference near 0, heterozygous near a half, homozygous alternate near 1), so a wrong column pair is obvious to a reader but not to the engine. Cross-checked with an independent formulation (SUM/COUNT over read_depth as the denominator, the samples filter as an IN subquery, LOW_QUAL excluded by inequality): identical. trapSql divides read depth by total reads, the duplicate pair: verified 1.000 for all three genotypes. The question states the high-confidence and depth qualifiers, so this case isolates the column-pair trap from the metric definition; allele-fraction-by-significance is the variant that leaves them to the metric. Rows are compared by the result set; no text check, because the genotype labels are already in the question.

Trap query (must return different rows): SELECT call.genotype, ROUND(AVG(call.read_depth * 1.0 / call.total_read_count), 3) AS mean_allele_fraction FROM genomics.variant_calls call JOIN genomics.samples sample ON sample.id = call.sample_id WHERE sample.is_control = false AND call.filter_status = 'PASS' AND call.total_read_count >= 20 GROUP BY call.genotype ORDER BY call.genotype

Paraphrases: For each genotype, what is the mean fraction of reads supporting the alternate allele on high-confidence calls with a depth of 20 or more? Three decimal places, please. | Looking only at high-confidence calls covered by at least 20 reads, how does the average alternate-allele fraction compare across genotypes, to three decimals?

Moved from feat/engine-eval-loop (branch category ratio-trap, provenance model-drafted-verified).

cases.question: What is the average alternate-allele fraction for each pathogenicity class, to three decimal places?
cases.intent: The same alt/total ratio on a different grouping that needs the variants join, with the allele_fraction qualifiers left to the metric definition.
cases.notes:
Verified against the live fixture (controls out; PASS calls with total reads >= 20, per the allele_fraction metric): 5 rows — BENIGN 0.425, LIKELY_BENIGN 0.432, LIKELY_PATHOGENIC 0.423, PATHOGENIC 0.283, VUS 0.416. cases.question: How do our variants break down across genome assemblies?
cases.intent: Group by a column that has exactly one value — the answer has to say so instead of presenting 100% as a finding.
cases.notes:
assembly is 'GRCh38' on all 450 variants (the CHECK constraint allows nothing else). The breakdown is one row, and the useful answer states that every variant is on a single assembly rather than dressing a constant up as a distribution. Guards against reporting a one-row group-by as if it were a comparison. No trapSql, deliberately: the failure is in the prose (presenting the one-row breakdown as a distribution, or inventing GRCh37), and every plausible query returns the same single GRCh38 row, so a trap would be vacuous by construction. The includes check and the judge carry the case.

Paraphrases: What is the split of our variants by reference genome build? | How many variants do we have on each genome assembly?

Moved from feat/engine-eval-loop (branch category constant-column, provenance hand).

expectedSql.postgres: SELECT variant.assembly, COUNT(*) AS variants FROM genomics.variants variant GROUP BY variant.assembly ORDER BY variant.assembly

cases.judgeRubric: The fixture stores only one genome assembly: every one of the 450 variants is GRCh38. The correct answer says that all variants are on GRCh38, so there is no assembly breakdown to compare. Score pass=true only if the final answer states that all variants are on a single assembly (GRCh38) and therefore that there is no breakdown to compare — reporting the count (450) or "100%" is fine as long as the answer says the column is constant. Score pass=false if it presents the single value as a meaningful distribution, invents a second assembly (e.g. GRCh37/hg19) or implies a comparison the data cannot support. Close but wrong: an answer that shows "GRCh38: 450 (100%)" as a breakdown without saying the column holds a single value, or that says "mostly GRCh38" as if other assemblies were present — that must FAIL.

cases.question: How are our pathogenic variants split across genome builds?
cases.intent: Break a filtered set down by a column that holds one value — the answer has to say there is only one build, not present 100% as a split.
cases.notes:
Verified against the live fixture: 96 pathogenic variants, all on GRCh38 (assembly is GRCh38 on all 450 variants; the CHECK constraint allows nothing else). Cross-checked with an independent formulation (a per-assembly FILTER count summed back up): identical, 96. The reference returns the figure only, not the assembly column: the dataset knowledge tells the agent not to group by assembly, so a correct answer may run a plain count and name GRCh38 in prose — a reference carrying the assembly column would fail that answer as narrower. The build name is checked by the includes check, the behaviour by the judge. No trapSql: the failure is narrative (a one-row split presented as a distribution, or an invented GRCh37 share), and every plausible query returns the same single figure, so a trap would be vacuous by construction. The genomics fixture has exactly one constant column (assembly); this case and pathogenic-share-by-assembly reach it through a filter and a rate, so a fix keyed to the exact wording of variants-by-assembly still fails here.

Paraphrases: What is the genome-build breakdown of our pathogenic variants? | Across reference genome assemblies, how many pathogenic variants do we have on each?

Moved from feat/engine-eval-loop (branch category constant-column, provenance model-drafted-verified).

expectedSql.postgres: SELECT COUNT(*) AS pathogenic_variants FROM genomics.variants variant WHERE variant.clinical_significance = 'PATHOGENIC'

cases.judgeRubric: The fixture stores one genome build: every variant, and so each of the 96 pathogenic variants, is on GRCh38. The correct answer says all 96 pathogenic variants are on GRCh38 and that there is no split across builds to report. Score pass=true only if the final answer states that the pathogenic variants are all on a single build (GRCh38) and that no other build is present — giving the count (96) or "100%" is fine as long as the answer says the build never varies. Score pass=false if it presents a split between builds, invents a second build (e.g. GRCh37/hg19) or a lift-over figure, or implies a comparison the data cannot support. Close but wrong: an answer that shows "GRCh38: 96 (100%)" as a breakdown table without saying it is the only build, or that says "mostly GRCh38" as if other builds were present — that must FAIL.

cases.question: Does the share of variants classified as pathogenic differ between genome assemblies? Give the percentage for each assembly to one decimal place.
cases.intent: A comparison question over a constant column: the honest answer is that there is only one assembly, so there is nothing to compare.
cases.notes:
Verified against the live fixture: 21.3% (96 of 450 variants are pathogenic), all on GRCh38 — the only assembly. Cross-checked with an independent formulation (AVG of a 100/0 indicator restricted to assembly = GRCh38): identical, 21.3. The reference returns the percentage only, for the same reason as pathogenic-variants-by-assembly: an answer that computes the share without grouping by the constant column and names GRCh38 in prose is correct. No trapSql — narrative trap, vacuous in SQL by construction (a GROUP BY assembly returns the same single 21.3 row). The question presumes a comparison exists; the judge checks the answer declines it rather than dressing one row up as a finding.

Paraphrases: Is the pathogenic share of our variants higher on one genome build than another? Percentage per build, to one decimal place. | Compare the percentage of variants that are pathogenic across reference genome assemblies, to one decimal place.

Moved from feat/engine-eval-loop (branch category constant-column, provenance model-drafted-verified).

expectedSql.postgres: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(CASE WHEN variant.clinical_significance = 'PATHOGENIC' THEN 1 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pathogenic_pct FROM genomics.variants variant

cases.judgeRubric: The fixture stores one genome assembly: all 450 variants are GRCh38, and 96 of them (21.3%) are pathogenic. The correct answer says there is only one assembly (GRCh38), so the share cannot differ between assemblies, and gives the pathogenic share on it (21.3%). Score pass=true only if the final answer states that every variant is on GRCh38 (a single assembly) and that no between-assembly comparison is possible — giving the 21.3% figure is fine. Score pass=false if it presents a comparison, invents a figure for another assembly (GRCh37/hg19 or any other), or says the share is the same or different across assemblies as if several were present. Close but wrong: an answer that reports "GRCh38: 21.3%" as a per-assembly table without saying it is the only assembly, or that concludes "the share does not differ between assemblies" without saying there is only one — that must FAIL.

cases.question: How many of our variants have a dbSNP rsID?
cases.intent: Count the populated rows of a mostly-null column instead of grouping by it.
cases.notes:
rsid is non-null on only 46 of 450 variants (10.2%), so grouping by rsid buries 404 variants under a blank key and a per-rsid breakdown is 47 near-useless groups. The answer must be the count of variants that HAVE an identifier — checked by the result set, not by a text match on 46. Guards against the engine presenting the null group as a finding. trapSql groups by the identifier itself: verified 47 rows, a blank key holding 404 variants plus 46 singletons, against the reference single row of 46.

Trap query (must return different rows): SELECT variant.rsid, COUNT(*) AS variants FROM genomics.variants variant GROUP BY variant.rsid ORDER BY variants DESC, variant.rsid

Paraphrases: How many variants are catalogued with a dbSNP identifier? | What number of our variants carry an rs number from dbSNP?

Moved from feat/engine-eval-loop (branch category empty-column, provenance hand).

expectedSql.postgres: SELECT COUNT(*) AS variants_with_rsid FROM genomics.variants variant WHERE variant.rsid IS NOT NULL

cases.question: Within each pathogenicity class, what percentage of variants have a dbSNP rsID, to one decimal place?
cases.intent: Count the populated values of a mostly-null column inside each group; the empty rows stay in the denominator.
cases.notes:
Verified against the live fixture (46 of 450 variants have an rsID): 5 rows — BENIGN 10.3 (7 of 68), LIKELY_BENIGN 8.1 (6 of 74), LIKELY_PATHOGENIC 9.4 (5 of 53), PATHOGENIC 6.3 (6 of 96), VUS 13.8 (22 of 159). Cross-checked with an independent formulation (per-class totals LEFT JOINed to per-class counts of rsid ~ '^rs'): identical. trapSql filters the empty rows out first and so answers the inverted question (which class the rsID variants fall in): verified BENIGN 15.2, LIKELY_BENIGN 13.0, LIKELY_PATHOGENIC 10.9, PATHOGENIC 13.0, VUS 47.8 — the null rows silently left the denominator. Percentages are compared by the result set.

Trap query (must return different rows): SELECT variant.clinical_significance, ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (), 1) AS pct_with_rsid FROM genomics.variants variant WHERE variant.rsid IS NOT NULL GROUP BY variant.clinical_significance ORDER BY variant.clinical_significance

Paraphrases: For each ACMG classification, what share of its variants carry a dbSNP identifier? Percentages to one decimal place. | How well is each pathogenicity class covered by dbSNP — what percentage of its variants have an rs number, to one decimal?

Moved from feat/engine-eval-loop (branch category empty-column, provenance model-drafted-verified).

expectedSql.postgres: SELECT variant.clinical_significance, ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(variant.rsid) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_with_rsid FROM genomics.variants variant GROUP BY variant.clinical_significance ORDER BY variant.clinical_significance

cases.question: Which genes carry exactly seven pathogenic variants?
cases.intent: A HAVING-style question whose answer is a tie, so no arbitrary tie-break can hide.
cases.notes:
MLH1 and PTEN both carry exactly 7 PATHOGENIC variants; TP53 is the only gene above that, with 11. A 'top genes by pathogenic variants' phrasing would let a LIMIT 1 silently drop one of the tied genes, so the question asks for the tie explicitly and both symbols must appear. Guards against answers that report one arbitrary winner from a tied group. trapSql keeps one row of the tie (LIMIT 1): verified MLH1 7 alone, against the reference MLH1 7 and PTEN 7.

Trap query (must return different rows): SELECT gene.hgnc_symbol AS gene, COUNT(*) AS pathogenic_variants FROM genomics.variants variant JOIN genomics.genes gene ON gene.id = variant.gene_id WHERE variant.clinical_significance = 'PATHOGENIC' GROUP BY gene.hgnc_symbol HAVING COUNT(*) = 7 ORDER BY pathogenic_variants DESC, gene.hgnc_symbol LIMIT 1

Paraphrases: Which genes have precisely 7 variants classified as pathogenic? | List every gene with exactly seven pathogenic variants.

Moved from feat/engine-eval-loop (branch category ties, provenance hand).

cases.question: Which ancestry group has the most subjects?
cases.intent: A plain "which is largest" question whose answer is a three-way tie, so a LIMIT 1 silently drops two correct groups.
cases.notes:
Verified against the live fixture: three ancestry groups tie on 10 subjects — LWK (Luhya in Webuye, Kenya), PNG (Papuan Highlanders), YRI (Yoruba in Ibadan, Nigeria); JPT is next on 9. Counts are over all 120 subjects (the control flag is on samples, not subjects). Cross-checked with an independent formulation (DENSE_RANK over a LEFT JOIN from ancestry_groups): identical, 3 rows of 10. The reference returns the tied counts only — ancestry groups have both a code and a name and either is a correct way to name them, so the identities are checked by the text pattern (code or name for each of the three) and the result set checks that exactly three groups share the top count. trapSql is the tempting ORDER BY … LIMIT 1: verified one row, Papuan Highlanders 10. Unlike genes-with-seven-pathogenic the question does not ask for the tie, which is what makes it hard.

Trap query (must return different rows): SELECT ancestry.name AS ancestry_group, COUNT(*) AS subjects FROM genomics.subjects subject JOIN genomics.ancestry_groups ancestry ON ancestry.id = subject.ancestry_group_id GROUP BY ancestry.name ORDER BY subjects DESC LIMIT 1

Paraphrases: What is our largest ancestry group by number of subjects? | Which ancestry group has the largest number of enrolled subjects?

Moved from feat/engine-eval-loop (branch category ties, provenance model-drafted-verified).

cases.question: How many damaging variants did we find?
cases.intent: Map a clinician's word onto the enum the column actually stores.
cases.notes:
There is no 'DAMAGING' value. clinical_significance is PATHOGENIC (96), LIKELY_PATHOGENIC (53), VUS (159), LIKELY_BENIGN (74) or BENIGN (68); 'damaging' is the ACMG pair PATHOGENIC + LIKELY_PATHOGENIC = 149. An answer that matches the literal word returns 0, and one that counts PATHOGENIC alone returns 96. The count is checked by the result set; the likely-pathogenic word check asks the answer to say it folded that class in. Guards against both the empty-filter and the half-filter failures. trapSql is the half filter (PATHOGENIC only): verified 96 against the reference 149.

Trap query (must return different rows): SELECT COUNT(*) AS damaging_variants FROM genomics.variants variant WHERE variant.clinical_significance = 'PATHOGENIC'

Paraphrases: How many harmful variants are in our data? | What is the total number of damaging variants we have identified?

Moved from feat/engine-eval-loop (branch category value-vocabulary, provenance hand).

expectedSql.postgres: SELECT COUNT(*) AS damaging_variants FROM genomics.variants variant WHERE variant.clinical_significance IN ('PATHOGENIC', 'LIKELY_PATHOGENIC')

The count is checked by the result set; the splice check asks the answer to say it folded the splice-site classes in, like damaging-variant-count does for likely pathogenic.

cases.question: How many samples did we sequence in 2015?
cases.intent: The cohort was collected in 2023 and 2024 only — the agent must say so instead of returning a confident zero or inventing a figure.
cases.notes:
samples.collected_on spans 2023-02-02 to 2024-12-11 (68 samples in 2023, 72 in 2024) and a CHECK constraint forbids anything else. A bare 'zero' is technically true but useless and reads like a finding; the honest answer names the covered window. noToolErrors was retired (no reference SQL, and a coverage probe that errors is not a wrong answer); didNotCall create_visual stays as the one tool check — charting a year with no data is always wrong. Guards against silently answering outside the fixture's coverage.

Moved from feat/engine-eval-loop (branch category out-of-scope, provenance hand).
cases.judgeRubric: The question asks about 2015, a year this cohort does not cover: every sample was collected between 2023-02-02 and 2024-12-11. The correct answer says there are no 2015 samples and that the cohort was collected in 2023 and 2024. Score pass=true only if the final answer makes clear there is no 2015 data AND explicitly states the period the data DOES cover (2023 and/or 2024), without inventing any 2015 sample count, sequencing run or statistic. Score pass=false if it reports a 2015 figure as if it were a real measurement, presents a bare '0' with no statement of what the data covers, or fabricates any claim about sequencing done in 2015. Close but wrong: an answer that says "0 samples were sequenced in 2015" with no covered period, or one that names the covered years but then presents a 2023 or 2024 count as the answer to the 2015 question — that must FAIL.

cases.question: What is the average DNA methylation level of BRCA1 across our samples?
cases.intent: The dataset measures variants and expression, not methylation — the agent must say so instead of inventing a level or passing expression off as methylation.
cases.notes:
There is no methylation entity or column anywhere in the schema: the per-sample measurements are variant calls (genotype, read counts, filter status, genotype quality) and gene expression (raw_count and tpm per gene per sample; BRCA1 averages 98.742 TPM over the non-control samples). The tempting failure is to answer with expression and call it methylation, or to "infer" methylation from low expression. didNotCall create_visual is the one tool check (charting a measure that does not exist is always wrong); no reference SQL.

Moved from feat/engine-eval-loop (branch category out-of-scope, provenance model-drafted-verified).
